findings.claim: formatRelativeAge picks a unit by fixed day thresholds: 30-day months below 365 days, then 365-day years. A book added 360 to 364 days ago therefore reads "12 months ago" / "12か月前" instead of "1 year ago". 28 to 29 days reads "4 weeks ago". The tests do not cover any boundary (they check 3, 14, 240 and 730 days only).
findings.impact: In normal use the relative-age line on a Reading card can show the odd "12 months ago" for about 5 days a year per book. This is cosmetic and is not a wrong date order.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/format.ts:39-41: `if (diffDay < 30) weeks; if (diffDay < 365) return text(-Math.floor(diffDay / 30), "month"); return years`. For diffDay=360, Math.floor(360/30)=12, so the result is month -12. frontend/src/lib/__tests__/format.test.ts:58-62 covers no boundary values.
findings.repro: Work through format.ts:40 by hand with diffDay 360: floor(360/30)=12, which gives Intl.RelativeTimeFormat('en').format(-12,'month') = "12 months ago".

bucket_proposal.reason: Cosmetic wording at a unit boundary. I29 requires a relative age, and the output is still relative.
